Managed Apps listing copy vs MDM engineering — two different jobs

Teams assume MDM app install or Managed App Configuration support covers storefront language. MDM runtime and App Store Connect actually separate fleet deployment from product-page copy:

  • Managed Apps on the device — when MDM pushes, installs, removes, or updates apps on supervised or enrolled devices, applies Managed App Configuration payloads, enforces required apps, or manages app blacklist and whitelist policies. System MDM app lifecycle — outside AppLocale scope.
  • MDM console and server flows — IT admins assign apps, configure AppConfig dictionaries, set per-app VPN, enable silent install, and manage required-app policies from Jamf, Intune, Kandji, Mosyle, or your app's fleet dashboard. MDM schema and server work belong in engineering — not listing rewrite.
  • Managed Apps marketing on the product page — description paragraphs, subtitle positioning, keywords, promotional text, and screenshot overlays that tell buyers your app supports MDM app install, Managed App Configuration, silent install, required apps, managed open-in, or per-app VPN association. Connect text fields — this page.
  • Pricing and Availability → China — makes the app downloadable on the China storefront. Separate from language rows.
  • App Store tab → Chinese (Simplified) localization — independent row for title, subtitle, keywords, description, promotional text, and screenshot caption lines. Empty or English here means China buyers see English fallback regardless of Managed Apps claims in the app.

An app that deploys Managed Apps to fleets and a localized China listing are both valuable — neither replaces the other. AppLocale covers how you describe MDM app install, Managed App Configuration, and silent install workflows on the store page, not whether your code pushes apps at runtime.

Managed Apps vs VPP, Custom Apps, and Configuration Profiles — hard disambiguation

Apple groups several organization deployment surfaces. Indie teams conflate them on one product page. AppLocale covers Managed Apps and Managed App Configuration marketing on listing metadata — not volume licensing, private distribution, or .mobileconfig profile payloads as lead:

  • Managed Apps (this page) — MDM push, install, remove, and update of apps on supervised or enrolled devices; Managed App Configuration (AppConfig), managed open-in, per-app VPN association, silent install, required apps, and app blacklist or whitelist. Gallery frames may show "Managed Apps", "Silent install", "Required apps", "Managed App Configuration", or app-deployment dashboards. zh-Hans terms: 托管应用, 管理式应用, 应用配置, Managed App Configuration, MDM 应用分发, 静默安装, 必需应用.
  • Volume Purchase / Apps and Books (different) — organization bulk purchase and volume licensing of App Store app licenses — 批量购买 vocabulary. VPP buys seats; Managed Apps deploys and configures apps already licensed or assigned. See VPP / Apps and Books listing when volume license procurement is your lead — not MDM app install.
  • Custom Apps / Unlisted private distribution (different) — org-scoped apps distributed to specific organizations through ABM or ASM — not public MDM app push and update on enrolled store-listed apps. See Unlisted & Custom App listing when private org distribution is your lead — not Managed Apps deployment.
  • Configuration Profiles (different) — installable .mobileconfig payload files that deliver Wi-Fi, VPN, certificates, restrictions, email, and other settings broadly — 配置描述文件 vocabulary. Managed App Configuration is app-scoped config delivered through MDM to a specific managed app — not a general .mobileconfig profile editor. See Configuration Profiles listing when .mobileconfig profile payloads and Wi-Fi/VPN profile distribution are your lead — not Managed Apps app lifecycle.

Your gallery may show a silent install flow on one frame and a VPP redemption screen on the next — but listing copy should name each claim accurately per frame. A Managed Apps badge is not a volume-purchase pitch, not a Custom App distribution walkthrough, and not a Wi-Fi 描述文件 payload editor unless that is what the screenshot shows.

Managed Apps–specific vocabulary — what translates differently in zh-Hans

Managed Apps and MDM app-deployment marketing on App Store pages uses vocabulary general localization guides rarely cover. zh-Hans copy should reflect how Chinese App Store readers evaluate Managed Apps — not a literal paste of US marketing:

托管应用 / 管理式应用 (Managed Apps)

Apple's Chinese MDM and enterprise support materials use 托管应用 and 管理式应用 for apps installed and managed through MDM on supervised or enrolled devices. Some technical marketing also uses 托管 App on frames that show app-deployment dashboards. AppLocale picks the term IT admins recognize on each screenshot.

应用配置 / Managed App Configuration

Managed App Configuration — often called AppConfig in MDM docs — delivers app-scoped key-value settings to managed apps through MDM. zh-Hans marketing uses 应用配置 alongside Managed App Configuration when your English source uses AppConfig terminology — distinct from general 配置描述文件 Configuration Profile payloads.

MDM 应用分发 (MDM app distribution)

US pages use "MDM app install" or "Push apps to managed devices." China storefront copy often uses MDM 应用分发 when describing push, install, remove, and update workflows for fleet app consistency — separate from VPP 批量购买 license procurement.

静默安装 (silent install)

When MDM installs apps without prompting the user on supervised devices, zh-Hans enterprise docs use 静默安装. Use this term when your English source markets silent or unattended app install — not generic "one-tap install" consumer language.

必需应用 (required apps)

Policies that require specific apps remain installed on managed devices map to 必需应用 in zh-Hans MDM documentation. Use when your gallery shows required-app enforcement dashboards — distinct from consumer "must-have apps" marketing.

Managed open-in and per-app VPN

Managed open-in controls which apps may receive documents from a managed app; per-app VPN routes traffic for a specific managed app through an org VPN tunnel. zh-Hans copy may keep Managed open-in and Per-app VPN on technical frames — with brief native benefit lines where Chinese IT admins expect them.

App blacklist / whitelist

MDM policies that block or allow specific apps on managed devices. zh-Hans fleet-admin copy may describe 应用黑名单 and 应用白名单 when your English source shows blacklist or whitelist UI — distinct from consumer parental-control marketing unless that is your genuine scope.

Subtitle and keyword packing

The 30-character subtitle and 100-character keyword field need MDM search terms Chinese buyers type — see Simplified Chinese keywords & subtitle for field mechanics. Terms like 托管应用, 应用配置, and 静默安装 each signal different intent from 批量购买 (VPP), Custom App private distribution, or 配置描述文件 keywords.

Caption lines vs burned-in badges

Marketing screenshot overlays you control — "Managed Apps" or "Silent install" headlines on gallery frames — are separate caption fields or burned-in PNG text. See Screenshot captions in Simplified Chinese for caption-field mechanics when overlays are editable in Connect.

AppLocale FAQ

What are Apple Managed Apps and why does listing copy matter?

Managed Apps covers MDM push, install, remove, and update of apps on supervised or enrolled devices, plus Managed App Configuration, silent install, required apps, and app blacklist or whitelist policies. Marketing those workflows on your en-US page does not auto-fill zh-Hans Connect fields.

Does MDM app install or Managed App Configuration support auto-translate my China listing?

No. Managed Apps and AppConfig are runtime MDM workflows — they do not create or fill a Simplified Chinese localization row. Empty or English zh-Hans fields mean China buyers see en-US fallback on the product page.

What listing fields does AppLocale rewrite for Managed Apps apps?

Paste-ready Simplified Chinese (zh-Hans) copy for App Store Connect listing fields you specify: title, subtitle, keywords, description, promotional text when included, and screenshot overlay or caption lines that mention Managed Apps, MDM app install, Managed App Configuration, or silent install — rewritten from your English originals with terms like 托管应用, 应用配置, and 静默安装 where accurate.

How is this different from VPP, Custom Apps, or Configuration Profiles?

Managed Apps listing copy markets MDM app install, update, and Managed App Configuration on enrolled devices. VPP listing copy markets organization bulk license purchase. Custom Apps listing copy markets private org-scoped distribution. Configuration Profile listing copy markets installable .mobileconfig payload files broadly. Listing vocabulary must follow your English lead feature.

How is this different from Managed Apple ID, Enterprise SSO, or Certificate Management?

Managed Apps deploys and configures apps on devices. Managed Apple ID is org-account identity. Enterprise SSO authenticates users to apps and services. Certificate Management enrolls and renews PKI credentials. Each is a separate Apple feature — do not reuse boilerplate across them.

No. We deliver listing metadata copy only. MDM server deployment and AppConfig payload engineering are outside AppLocale scope. We rewrite how you describe existing Managed Apps workflows on the store page — we do not push apps to fleets at runtime.

What character limits apply to zh-Hans Managed Apps fields?

App name and subtitle are each up to 30 characters. Keywords allow up to 100 characters. Description and screenshot caption lines have longer limits but should stay concise — especially overlays that must fit on-device mockups.
